newsitem.title: FRANCE: Founder leaves Canal Plus supervisory board.
newsitem.headline: Founder leaves Canal Plus supervisory board.

text.p: Andre Rousselet, the founder of French pay-television company Canal PLus SA on Monday said he was leaving the supervisory board because he feared "interference" in the company's decision making.
He told Reuters he made his decision following a February 6 deal under which Generale des Eaux transferred its 19.3 percent stake in Canal Plus to Havas in exchange for shares in Havas.
It also bought Havas shares from Alcatel Alsthom bringing its total stake in the media, advertising and travel group to 20 percent.
Havas will have a 36.6 percent stake in Canal Plus after the planned merger of the television group with Nethold, and 40 percent if the stake of allied bank Societe Generale is added.

"(My departure) is not entirely unrelated to the recent developments that have taken place, in particular the increasingly important role of Generale des Eaux in Havas and of Havas in Canal Plus," he said in a telephone interview.
"I believed that I had no longer a place in such a supervisory board," he said, adding he had informed Canal Plus chairman and chief executive Pierre Lescure in a letter of his decision.

He added that the latest decision to leave the company he founded in 1984 was "in fact the consequence of the shareholders' pact" of Havas, Generale des Eaux and Societe Generale which led to his ousting as chairman and chief executive in 1995.
He said he had some fears about the future of the group which has become a leading player in the European television sector.

"I do not know whether the independence of Canal Plus is being threathened. I can only say that if it were threatened, I would be unable to respond to the wish of independence that the staff of Canal Plus would still hope to have," he said.
He said that the rising power of Generale des Eaux in the audiovisual sector was "not healthy".

"Up to now the success of Canal Plus is mainly due to the independence of its management. From the moment that this independence is put into question, one can say that there is a risk to see interference in the future of Canal Plus of interests that are not directly related to the future of the pay-television company," he said.
